Famous for world-class dry powder snow skiing in winter and blooming lupins and daisies in summer, alongside the historic 1915 Maharani Temple atop its central knoll.
Jammu and Kashmir.timings: Gondola: 09:00 AM - 04:00 PM (Requires advance online booking)
Jammu and Kashmir.entryFee: Phase 1: ₹740; Phase 2 (Apharwat): ₹950 (Official J&K Cable Car portal)
Jammu and Kashmir.bestTimeToVisit: December to March (Powder Skiing) | May to September (Flower Meadows)
subtypes: Pir Panjal High Altitude Alpine Meadow & Ski Bowl

sources.title: Jammu and Kashmir State Tourism & Statutory Gazetteer

Jammu and Kashmir.imageAlt: Snow-blanketed slopes and pine forests of Gulmarg with the Apharwat peak cable car in the distance
highlights: Gulmarg Gondola (World's 2nd Highest Operating Cable Car at 3,980m)
Apharwat Peak Snow Bowl & Frozen Alpather Glacial Lake
Asia's Premier Dry Powder Ski Slopes
Historic Maharani Shiva Temple atop Gulmarg Central Knoll

Jammu and Kashmir.name: Pahalgam (Valley of Shepherds) & Lidder River
alternateNames: Traditional Starting Basecamp for the Holy Amarnath Yatra
Sub-Alpine Betaab Valley & Aru Valley Meadows
Jammu and Kashmir.subcategory: Confluence Valley, Lidder Gorge & Amarnath Parikrama Base
Jammu and Kashmir.description: Located at 2,130 meters at the confluence of the Lidder River and Sheshnag streams, Pahalgam ('Valley of Shepherds') serves as the traditional starting basecamp for the annual holy Amarnath Cave Yatra via Chandanwari. Encircled by dense pine forests and snow-capped peaks, it features the picturesque sub-alpine Betaab Valley (named after the Bollywood film shot here), pristine Aru Valley, and the 12th-century stone Mamaleshwar Shiva Temple.
Jammu and Kashmir.bestTimeToVisit: April to October (Chilly winters with snow)
subtypes: Confluence Valley, Lidder Gorge & Amarnath Parikrama Base

sources.title: Jammu and Kashmir State Tourism & Statutory Gazetteer

Jammu and Kashmir.imageAlt: Turquoise Lidder river rushing through the verdant pine valleys of Pahalgam, Kashmir
highlights: Traditional Starting Basecamp for the Holy Amarnath Yatra
Sub-Alpine Betaab Valley & Aru Valley Meadows
Crystal-Clear Turquoise Lidder River Trout Waters

Jammu and Kashmir.name: Wular Lake (India's Largest Freshwater Lake & Ramsar Site)
Jammu and Kashmir.description: Surrounded by snow-capped Himalayan peaks in the Kashmir Valley, Wular Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia, fed by the Jhelum River. Designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance, it provides vital habitat for millions of migratory waterfowl, water chestnut (Singhara) harvesting, and the historic Zaina Lank island built by Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin.

sources.title: Jammu and Kashmir State Tourism & Statutory Gazetteer

Jammu and Kashmir.imageAlt: Vast open freshwater expanse of Wular Lake surrounded by Himalayan mountains in Kashmir

Manipur.name: Loktak Lake & Keibul Lamjao (Floating National Park)
alternateNames: World's Only Floating National Park (Keibul Lamjao)
Manipur.description: The largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous worldwide for its unique 'Phumdis'—heterogeneous masses of floating organic vegetation and soil. The southern portion comprises Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park on Earth and the exclusive habitat of the endangered Sangai brow-antlered deer.
Manipur.imageAlt: Circular floating biomass phumdis and calm expanse of Loktak Lake, Manipur
highlights: World's Only Floating National Park (Keibul Lamjao)

Odisha.name: Chilika Lake & Nalabana Bird Sanctuary
alternateNames: Over 160 Migratory Bird Species at Nalabana
Odisha.description: Sprawling across 1,100 sq km along the Bay of Bengal coast in Odisha. Asia's largest brackish water lagoon, declared a Ramsar wetland. Famous for sheltering over a million migratory birds each winter and one of only two lagoons in the world home to endangered Irrawaddy dolphins.
Odisha.bestTimeToVisit: November to February (Peak migratory bird season)
Odisha.imageAlt: Serene waters of Chilika lagoon with wading birds and distant fishing boats, Odisha
highlights: Over 160 Migratory Bird Species at Nalabana

Odisha.name: Konark Sun Temple (Black Pagoda)
Odisha.description: 13th-century monumental stone chariot conceived by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty. Sculpted with 24 carved stone sundial wheels drawn by seven galloping horses, engineered as an architectural hymn to Surya.
Odisha.imageAlt: Ornate carved 24-spoke stone wheel sundial of Konark Sun Temple chariot, Odisha

Odisha.name: Puri Golden Beach & Swargadwar
Odisha.subcategory: Blue Flag Certified Sacred Pilgrim Shore
Odisha.description: The sacred shoreline of the Bay of Bengal at Jagannath Puri, awarded the prestigious Blue Flag certification for eco-cleanliness. Millions of pilgrims take holy dips in Mahodadhi (the sacred ocean) before offering prayers to Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra.
Odisha.imageAlt: Sacred sunrise waves breaking along the Blue Flag certified Golden Beach, Puri

Odisha.name: Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves (ASI Jain Monasteries)
Odisha.description: Situated on two adjacent sandstone hills on the outskirts of Bhubaneswar, these 33 rock-cut caves date back to the 2nd century BCE during the reign of King Kharavela of the Chedi dynasty. Udayagiri features the historic Hathigumpha Inscription (in Brahmi script) and the double-storeyed Rani Gumpha (Queen's Cave), while Khandagiri houses historic Jain shrines.
Odisha.asiMonumentId: ASI Bhubaneswar Circle Centrally Protected Monument

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India Gazette
sources.officialRecordId: ASI Bhubaneswar Circle Centrally Protected Monument

Odisha.imageAlt: Two-tiered pillared carved facade of Rani Gumpha cave at Udayagiri, Bhubaneswar

Odisha.name: Raghurajpur Heritage Crafts Village (Pattachitra & Gotipua)
alternateNames: Open-Door House Wall Murals along Village Lanes
Master Pattachitra & Tala Pattachitra (Palm Leaf Engraving)
Odisha.description: A rural heritage artisan village near Puri where every household is an active artist workshop. Renowned for ancient Pattachitra scroll paintings on treated cloth and dried palm leaves, cow dung toys, wooden masks, and as the birthplace of legendary Odissi guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and the traditional Gotipua precursor dance form.
Odisha.imageAlt: Vibrant painted walls and master artist working on traditional Pattachitra cloth scroll at Raghurajpur
highlights: Open-Door House Wall Murals along Village Lanes
Master Pattachitra & Tala Pattachitra (Palm Leaf Engraving)

Gujarat.name: Rani ki Vav (The Queen's Stepwell)
Gujarat.description: An exceptional subterranean water architecture marvel built in 1063 CE by Queen Udayamati of the Chaulukya dynasty. Designed as an inverted temple honoring sacred water, descending through seven stepped terraces adorned with over 500 principal sculptures of Lord Vishnu and his Dashavatara.
Gujarat.imageAlt: Seven terraced levels of carved sculpted pavilions inside Rani ki Vav stepwell, Patan

Gujarat.name: Sun Temple, Modhera & Surya Kund
alternateNames: Sabha Mandapa with 52 Carved Torana Pillars
Gujarat.description: Built in 1026 CE by King Bhima I of the Solanki Dynasty on the Tropic of Cancer. Engineered so that during the equinoxes, the first rays of the rising sun illuminate the sanctum's inner sun deity. Adjoined by the breathtaking stepped water reservoir 'Surya Kund' flanked by 108 miniature shrines.
Gujarat.timings: 07:00 AM - 06:00 PM (Light & Sound Show in Evening)
Gujarat.imageAlt: Geometrical stepped water tank of Surya Kund facing the ornate Sabha Mandap, Modhera
highlights: Sabha Mandapa with 52 Carved Torana Pillars

Gujarat.name: Gir National Park (Sole Asiatic Lion Habitat)
Gujarat.subcategory: Sole Global Sanctuary of the Asiatic Lion
Gujarat.description: The last remaining wild sanctuary of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) on Earth. Covering 1,412 sq km of dry teak deciduous forest in the Saurashtra peninsula, closely connected to the sacred Somnath Jyotirlinga circuit.
Gujarat.bestTimeToVisit: December to March (Closed June 16 to Oct 15)
Gujarat.imageAlt: Majestic male Asiatic Lion resting under the dry teak forest canopy of Sasan Gir

Gujarat.name: Manek Chowk Night Food Market, Ahmedabad
Gujarat.subcategory: Historic Old City Night Food Square
Gujarat.description: Located in the heart of UNESCO World Heritage City of Ahmedabad next to the historic tomb of Sultan Ahmed Shah. A bullion trading bazaar by day, it converts into a lively nocturnal food square serving chocolate-cheese sandwiches, Gwalior butter dosas, Ashrafi kulfis, and traditional Gujarati snacks.
Gujarat.imageAlt: Vibrant midnight food bazaar at historic Manek Chowk serving signature butter sandwiches and kulfi

Gujarat.name: Statue of Unity (Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel)
alternateNames: 153-Meter Viewing Gallery with Sardar Sarovar Dam Vistas
Gujarat.description: The world's tallest statue with a height of 182 meters (597 feet), twice the height of the Statue of Liberty, dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the Iron Man of India who united 562 princely states. Designed by master sculptor Ram V. Sutar and inaugurated in 2018 on Sadhu Bet island facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam on the sacred Narmada River. Features a high-speed elevator to the 153-meter chest viewing gallery accommodating 200 visitors simultaneously.
Gujarat.timings: 08:00 AM - 06:00 PM (Closed on Mondays for maintenance)
subtypes: World's Tallest Monument (182 meters)
Gujarat.imageAlt: Colossal 182-meter Statue of Unity rising above the Narmada River basin at Kevadia
highlights: 153-Meter Viewing Gallery with Sardar Sarovar Dam Vistas
Evening Laser Light & Projection Mapping Show

Gujarat.name: Great Rann of Kutch (White Salt Desert)
alternateNames: 7,500 sq km Sparkling Crystalline White Salt Flats
Full Moon Night Mirages over the Endless Horizon
Gujarat.subcategory: Seasonal Endless White Salt Marsh & Desert Safari
Gujarat.description: The largest seasonal salt marsh desert in the world, spanning over 7,505 square kilometers of shimmering white salt flats in the Thar Desert biome. Flooded during the monsoon by Arabian Sea tides and inland rivers, the waters evaporate by November to reveal an immaculate blinding-white salt crust extending to the horizon. Hosts the world-renowned 3-month Rann Utsav celebrating Kutchi handicrafts, camel caravans, and surreal full-moon desert nights.
Gujarat.entryFee: ₹100 (Adults) + ₹50 (Vehicle Permit) via Gujarat Police portal/Dhordo checkpost
Gujarat.bestTimeToVisit: November to February (Best on full moon nights)
subtypes: Seasonal Endless White Salt Marsh & Desert Safari
Gujarat.imageAlt: Endless crystalline white salt crust stretching towards the horizon in the Great Rann of Kutch
highlights: 7,500 sq km Sparkling Crystalline White Salt Flats
Full Moon Night Mirages over the Endless Horizon
Rann Utsav Kutchi Folk Music & Artisan Village
Flamingo City Protected Wetland Migratory Colony

Gujarat.name: Dholavira: A Harappan City (UNESCO)
Gujarat.description: One of the most remarkable and well-preserved urban settlements of the South Asian Bronze Age Harappan Civilization (3000-1500 BCE), situated on Khadir Bet island in the Great Rann of Kutch. Features a fortified citadel, ceremonial grounds, stepped water reservoirs, and world-renowned hydro-engineering systems.
Gujarat.asiMonumentId: ASI Western Circle Centrally Protected Site

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Convention Inscription
sources.officialRecordId: ASI Western Circle Centrally Protected Site

Gujarat.imageAlt: Ancient stone reservoir and masonry wall of Dholavira Harappan excavation site

Gujarat.name: Iranshah Atash Behram, Udvada (Supreme Zoroastrian Fire Temple)
Gujarat.subcategory: Supreme Sacred Zoroastrian Fire Temple (Consecrated 1742 CE)
Gujarat.description: The oldest and most prestigious of the eight Atash Behrams (highest grade of fire temple) in India, located in the peaceful coastal heritage town of Udvada. The sacred holy fire burning inside has been kept continuously alive for over 1,290 years, tracing back to the fire consecrated at Sanjan by Zoroastrian refugees following the fall of the Sasanian Empire.
Gujarat.imageAlt: Colonial Parsi heritage street architecture leading towards the Iranshah fire temple precinct in Udvada

Telangana.name: Golconda Fort & Acoustic Engineering
Telangana.description: Historic 16th-century fortress citadel built on a 120-meter granite hill. World-renowned as the trading center of the Golconda diamond mines that yielded the Koh-i-Noor and Hope diamonds. Famous for sophisticated acoustic architecture where a hand clap at the entrance portico is heard clearly at the Bala Hissar pavilion 1 km away.
Telangana.timings: 09:00 AM - 05:30 PM (Sound & Light Show in Evening)
Telangana.imageAlt: Outer stone bastions and gateway arches of historic Golconda Citadel, Hyderabad
highlights: Ramadasu Jail Cell with Stone Carvings

Telangana.name: Ramappa Temple (Rudreshwara, UNESCO)
Telangana.description: Built in 1213 CE under Kakatiya King Ganapati Deva by the master sculptor Ramappa (the only temple in India named after its architect). Engineered with floating light-weight porous bricks that float in water, built on a sandbox foundation to survive seismic earthquakes, and adorned with black basalt bracket figures.
Telangana.imageAlt: Intricately sculpted black basalt bracket figures and floating-brick shikhara at Ramappa

Telangana.name: Ramoji Film City (World's Largest Film Studio)
alternateNames: Interactive Movie Magic & Visual FX Show
Telangana.description: Sprawling over 2,000 acres, Ramoji Film City holds the Guinness World Record as the largest film studio complex in the world. Features interactive movie magic shows, stunt shows, thematic gardens, the iconic Baahubali grand set, and adventure amusement zones.
Telangana.imageAlt: Sprawling thematic movie sets and European fountains at Ramoji Film City, Hyderabad
highlights: Interactive Movie Magic & Visual FX Show

Telangana.name: Charminar & Laad Bazaar Pearl Quarter
alternateNames: Four 56-Meter Stately Minarets with Spiral Stairs
Oldest Surviving Mosque in Hyderabad on Upper Level
Telangana.subcategory: Qutb Shahi Granite Landmark & Historic Bazaar
Telangana.description: The square granite and lime-mortar monument and ceremonial gateway built in 1591 CE by Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah to commemorate the eradication of plague from the newly founded city of Hyderabad. Featuring four 56-meter grand minarets with 149 winding steps and an upper floor containing Hyderabad's oldest mosque. The monument stands at the heart of the historic Walled City, ringed by the glittering glass and lacquer bangle shops of Laad Bazaar.
Telangana.timings: 09:30 AM - 05:30 PM (Surrounding bazaar open till 10:00 PM)
Telangana.bestTimeToVisit: October to March (Evening for bazaar buzz)
subtypes: Qutb Shahi Granite Landmark & Historic Bazaar
Telangana.imageAlt: The four soaring minarets and ornate arches of the 1591 CE Charminar, Hyderabad
highlights: Four 56-Meter Stately Minarets with Spiral Stairs
Oldest Surviving Mosque in Hyderabad on Upper Level
Adjacent Laad Bazaar Centuries-Old Lacquer Bangles
Epicenter of Hyderabadi Haleem and Biryani Food Streets

Telangana.name: Pochampally Ikat Handloom Village (UNWTO Best Tourism Village)
alternateNames: UNWTO Best Tourism Village Heritage Walk
Telangana.subcategory: GI Certified Ikat Silk & UNWTO Tourism Village
Telangana.description: Globally celebrated as the 'Silk City of India' and awarded Best Tourism Village by the United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO). Pochampally is home to thousands of weaver households practicing ancient double-ikat tie-dye resist-weaving on traditional pit looms to craft exquisite geometric silk and cotton sarees.
Telangana.imageAlt: Master weaver operating a traditional wooden pit loom weaving geometric Pochampally Ikat silk
highlights: UNWTO Best Tourism Village Heritage Walk

Telangana.name: Hyderabad Charminar & Laad Bazaar Culinary Trail (GI Haleem & Dum Biryani)
Telangana.subcategory: GI Hyderabadi Haleem & Dum Biryani Heritage Corridor
Telangana.description: Radiating outwards from the 1591 CE Charminar monument, the Old City food quarter brings together culinary traditions of the Qutb Shahi and Asaf Jahi dynasties. Famous for authentic Kachchi Gosht Dum Biryani, GI-certified Hyderabadi Haleem slow-cooked with wheat and meat in bhattis, Osmania biscuits, and Irani Chai served in heritage tea cafes.
Telangana.imageAlt: Fragrant saffron-tinted Hyderabadi Dum Biryani served with mirchi ka salan and dahi chutney

Delhi.name: Red Fort & Qutub Minar Complex (UNESCO)
Delhi.subcategory: UNESCO World Heritage Delhi Monolithic Complexes
Delhi.description: Two pillars of Delhi's monumental heritage: The 73-meter fluted sandstone minaret of Qutub Minar (built in 1192 CE) adjacent to the rust-resistant 1,600-year-old Gupta Iron Pillar, alongside the monumental red sandstone ramparts of the Red Fort (Lal Qila) on the Yamuna.
Delhi.imageAlt: 73-meter fluted red sandstone and marble tower of Qutub Minar, Mehrauli New Delhi

Delhi.name: Lodhi Gardens & Historic Tombs
alternateNames: Bara Gumbad & Shisha Gumbad Medieval Domes
Delhi.description: A 90-acre lush city park in the diplomatic heart of New Delhi, blending landscape gardens with 15th-century Sayyid and Lodhi dynasty architectural monuments: Mohammed Shah's Tomb, Sikandar Lodi's Tomb, Shisha Gumbad, and Bara Gumbad.
Delhi.imageAlt: Bara Gumbad and domed 15th-century mausoleum set amidst landscaped rolling lawns, Delhi
highlights: Bara Gumbad & Shisha Gumbad Medieval Domes

Delhi.name: National Rail Museum, New Delhi
Delhi.description: Spanning 11 acres in Chanakyapuri, preserving India's 170-year railway heritage. Houses the Fairy Queen (1855, the world's oldest working steam locomotive), royal saloons of the Maharajas, steam simulators, and an operable joy train for families.
Delhi.imageAlt: Fairy Queen steam engine and royal vintage salon coaches preserved at National Rail Museum

Delhi.name: India Gate & National War Memorial
Delhi.nativeName: इण्डिया गेट एवं राष्ट्रीय समर स्मारक
alternateNames: National War Memorial 4 Concentric Concentric Chakras
Delhi.description: The soaring 42-meter triumphal arch standing at the eastern terminus of Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath) in New Delhi, designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens in 1921 to honor 84,000 soldiers who fell in the First World War and Third Anglo-Afghan War. Inscribed with 13,300 soldier names, the ceremonial complex is crowned by the black granite Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose canopy and integrated with the National War Memorial with its concentric Chakras of Sacrifice and Amar Jawan Jyoti eternal flame.
Delhi.timings: India Gate: Open 24 Hours | War Memorial: 09:00 AM - 09:00 PM
Delhi.entryFee: Free entry for all citizens and international visitors
subtypes: National Triumphal Arch & War Memorial
Delhi.imageAlt: India Gate illuminated against the twilight sky on Kartavya Path, New Delhi
highlights: National War Memorial 4 Concentric Concentric Chakras
Amar Jawan Jyoti Eternal Flame of Valour
Kartavya Path Lawns & Fountains Evening Promenade

Delhi.name: Humayun's Tomb & Sunder Nursery (UNESCO)
alternateNames: Architectural Precursor to the Taj Mahal
Delhi.description: The tomb of the Mughal Emperor Humayun, commissioned in 1558 CE by his first wife Empress Bega Begum and designed by Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas. The first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, it introduced the monumental double-dome and geometric Persian Charbagh layout that reached its zenith eighty years later in the Taj Mahal. Adjoins Sunder Nursery, a restored 90-acre UNESCO-awarded ecological heritage park.
subtypes: Mughal Garden Tomb & Charbagh Prototype
Delhi.imageAlt: Humayun's Tomb grand red sandstone facade and white marble dome flanked by Charbagh pools, Delhi
highlights: Architectural Precursor to the Taj Mahal

Delhi.name: Chandni Chowk Paranthe Wali Gali & Khari Baoli (Mughal Culinary Street)
Delhi.subcategory: Mughal Culinary Heritage & Asia's Largest Spice Market
Delhi.description: Laid out in 1650 by Mughal Princess Jahanara Begum, Chandni Chowk has been the culinary soul of Old Delhi for over 370 years. Famous for Paranthe Wali Gali with its 19th-century shops frying ghee-filled parathas, Natraj Dahi Bhalle (1940), historic jalebi corners, and Khari Baoli, recognized as Asia's largest historic wholesale spice bazaar.
Delhi.imageAlt: Golden deep-fried stuffed parathas served with pumpkin sabzi and mint chutney in Old Delhi

Delhi.name: National Museum, Janpath (Premier National Repository of Antiquities)
alternateNames: Sacred Piprahwa Relics of Lord Buddha
Delhi.subcategory: Premier National Museum of Art & Archaeology
Delhi.description: Established in 1949 on Janpath in New Delhi, the National Museum is India's premier cultural institution holding over 200,000 works of art spanning 5,000 years of civilization. Key galleries feature Indus Valley artifacts (the iconic Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro, Priest-King cast), Buddhist Art with relics of the Buddha from Piprahwa, Chola bronzes, and Mughal miniature paintings.
Delhi.imageAlt: Arched neoclassical gallery portico of the National Museum on Janpath, New Delhi
highlights: Sacred Piprahwa Relics of Lord Buddha

Andaman and Nicobar Islands.name: Radhanagar Beach (Beach No. 7), Havelock
Andaman and Nicobar Islands.description: Consistently ranked among the world's most pristine beaches, featuring fine powdery white sand, turquoise waters, and ancient tropical mahua rain trees along the Bay of Bengal in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

sources.title: Andaman and Nicobar Islands State Tourism & Statutory Gazetteer
sources.publisher: Andaman and Nicobar Islands Tourism Department

Andaman and Nicobar Islands.imageAlt: Crescent powdery white shoreline and tropical rainforest fringe at Radhanagar Beach, Havelock

Andaman and Nicobar Islands.name: Cellular Jail (Kala Pani National Memorial)
alternateNames: Colonial Panopticon Architecture with 7 Radiating Wings
Historic Solitary Confinement Cell of Veer Savarkar
Andaman and Nicobar Islands.subcategory: Colonial Solitary Confinement Prison & National Shrine
Andaman and Nicobar Islands.description: A monumental colonial prison complex constructed between 1896 and 1906 by the British regime to exile Indian freedom fighters and political dissidents to the remote Andaman archipelago (known dreaded as 'Kala Pani'). Built on a panopticon design with seven radiating three-storey wings housing 693 individual solitary confinement cells. Today a revered National Memorial featuring the cell of Veer Savarkar, an eternal flame (Swatantrya Jyoti), and a poignant evening sound and light presentation.
Andaman and Nicobar Islands.timings: 09:00 AM - 12:30 PM & 01:30 PM - 04:45 PM (Closed Mondays and National Holidays)
Andaman and Nicobar Islands.recommendedDuration: 2 to 3 Hours (Plus evening Sound & Light show)
subtypes: Colonial Solitary Confinement Prison & National Shrine

sources.title: Andaman and Nicobar Islands State Tourism & Statutory Gazetteer
sources.publisher: Andaman and Nicobar Islands Tourism Department

Andaman and Nicobar Islands.imageAlt: Central watchtower and radiating brick solitary wings of the historic Cellular Jail, Port Blair
highlights: Colonial Panopticon Architecture with 7 Radiating Wings
Historic Solitary Confinement Cell of Veer Savarkar
Swatantrya Jyoti Eternal Flame of National Freedom
Moving Evening Sound & Light Narrative on the Freedom Struggle

Lakshadweep.name: Agatti Island & Coral Lagoon
Lakshadweep.description: A 7.6 km long coral atoll in the Lakshadweep archipelago known for its breathtaking turquoise lagoons, vibrant living coral reefs, and white coral sand beaches. Accessible by airstrip with authorized tourism permits.
Lakshadweep.imageAlt: Translucent turquoise coral lagoon and white sand atoll of Agatti Island, Lakshadweep

Lakshadweep.name: Bangaram Atoll & Coral Reefs (Tear-Drop Lagoon)
alternateNames: Shallow Turquoise Coral Lagoon Enclosed by Barrier Reef
Lakshadweep.subcategory: Pristine Uninhabited Coral Atoll & Bioluminescent Lagoon
Lakshadweep.description: An idyllic teardrop-shaped uninhabited coral island spanning 0.5 square kilometers in the Union Territory of Lakshadweep, surrounded by an expansive shallow turquoise lagoon enclosed by a living barrier reef. Famed for its powder-soft white coral sands, nocturnal blue bioluminescent phytoplankton blooms that light up the surf, and world-class scuba diving offering encounters with green sea turtles, manta rays, reef sharks, and vibrant coral gardens.
Lakshadweep.timings: Resort access & boat transfers scheduled from Agatti Aerodrome
Lakshadweep.entryFee: Lakshadweep Administration Entry Permit required; package tariffs include permits
Lakshadweep.bestTimeToVisit: October to mid-May (Avoid monsoon choppy seas)
subtypes: Pristine Uninhabited Coral Atoll & Bioluminescent Lagoon
Lakshadweep.imageAlt: Turquoise shallow waters and powder white sands of the coral atoll at Bangaram, Lakshadweep
highlights: Shallow Turquoise Coral Lagoon Enclosed by Barrier Reef
PADI Scuba Diving with Sea Turtles and Manta Rays
Scenic Boat or Helicopter Transit from Agatti Aerodrome

Puducherry.name: Promenade Beach & French Quarter (White Town)
Puducherry.description: A 1.5 km scenic seaside promenade running alongside the Bay of Bengal, bordered by colonial Franco-Tamil architecture, the French War Memorial, Mahatma Gandhi statue, and the historic 18th-century French Quarter (White Town).
Puducherry.imageAlt: Cobblestone seaside boulevard and heritage French colonial buildings, White Town Pondicherry

Assam.name: Kaziranga National Park (UNESCO)
Assam.description: Located on the floodplains of the Brahmaputra River, Kaziranga shelters the world's largest population of the Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros (over 2,400 individuals), alongside Bengal Tigers, Wild Water Buffalo, and Asian Elephants in tall elephant grass marshes.
Assam.imageAlt: Solitary Great Indian One-Horned Rhinoceros grazing in tall wet elephant grass, Kaziranga

Assam.name: Majuli Island (World's Largest River Island)
Assam.description: The world's largest river island cradled by the mighty Brahmaputra River in Assam. The cultural nucleus of Neo-Vaishnavite traditions established by Srimanta Sankardeva in the 15th century, home to living monastic institutions (Satras) renowned for mask-making, Ankiya Nat drama, and Bhaona classical music.
Assam.bestTimeToVisit: October to March (Raas Mahotsav in November)
Assam.imageAlt: Tranquil Brahmaputra riverbank and traditional clay-and-bamboo mask workshops in Majuli

Assam.name: Moidams – Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty (UNESCO)
Assam.description: The royal burial mounds (Moidams) of the Tai-Ahom dynasty situated at the foothills of the Patkai Range at Charaideo, the first capital founded by King Chao Lung Siu-Ka-Pha in 1253 CE. Over 90 vaulted earthen mounds enshrine mortal remains of Ahom monarchs and queens, representing a unique architectural tradition preserved over 600 years.
Assam.asiMonumentId: ASI Guwahati Circle Centrally Protected Site

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Convention Inscription
sources.officialRecordId: ASI Guwahati Circle Centrally Protected Site

Assam.imageAlt: Vaulted green earthen tumulus burial mound of the Ahom monarchs at Charaideo, Assam

Assam.name: Sualkuchi Silk Village (Manchester of Assam & Golden Muga Silk)
alternateNames: GI Certified Golden Muga Silk Handlooms
Traditional Pit Loom & Fly Shuttle Weaving Guilds
Assam.subcategory: GI Certified Golden Muga & Eri Handloom Cluster
Assam.description: Situated on the northern bank of the Brahmaputra River, Sualkuchi is one of the world's largest handloom weaving villages, renowned as the 'Manchester of Assam'. Famous for indigenous wild silks including the lustrous golden Muga silk (endemic to Assam and protected with GI registration) and warm ahimsa Eri silk, woven on traditional jacquard throw-shuttle looms.
Assam.imageAlt: Traditional handloom weaving radiant golden Muga silk saree with red and black floral mekhela motifs
highlights: GI Certified Golden Muga Silk Handlooms
Traditional Pit Loom & Fly Shuttle Weaving Guilds

Uttarakhand.name: Jim Corbett National Park (India's First National Park)
Uttarakhand.description: Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, Corbett is India's oldest and most prestigious national park nestled along the Ramganga River in the Shivalik foothills. Home to Bengal Tigers, wild elephant herds, and over 580 resident bird species.
Uttarakhand.bestTimeToVisit: November to June (Dhikala zone opens Nov 15)
Uttarakhand.imageAlt: Dense sal forest canopy and Ramganga riverbed in Jim Corbett National Park, Uttarakhand

Uttarakhand.name: Valley of Flowers & Hemkund Sahib
Uttarakhand.description: High-altitude Himalayan valley nestled at 3,658 meters in Uttarakhand. Renowned for its endemic alpine flower meadows blooming from July to September, surrounded by snowcapped peaks and adjacent to the sacred high-altitude Hemkund Sahib glacial lake.
Uttarakhand.imageAlt: High-altitude Himalayan valley carpeted in endemic wildflowers below snowcapped peaks

Uttarakhand.name: Rishikesh White-Water Rafting & Ganga Ghats
alternateNames: 16 km Shivpuri to Rishikesh Rafting Stretch
Triveni Ghat Evening Maha Ganga Aarti
Uttarakhand.description: The Yoga Capital of the World where the sacred Ganga emerges from the Shivalik Himalayas into the plains. Famed for thrilling grade III & IV white-water river rafting from Shivpuri and Marine Drive, clifftop bungee jumping, and serene evening Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat.
Uttarakhand.bestTimeToVisit: September to June (Closed during monsoon rains)
Uttarakhand.imageAlt: Emerald Ganges rapids surging past Shivpuri with Himalayan bluffs in background, Rishikesh
highlights: 16 km Shivpuri to Rishikesh Rafting Stretch
Triveni Ghat Evening Maha Ganga Aarti
Ram Jhula & Laxman Jhula Suspension Bridges

Uttarakhand.name: Auli Bugyal & Nanda Devi Alpine Meadows (3,050 m)
alternateNames: 360° Panoramas of India's Highest Peaks (Nanda Devi, Trishul, Kamet)
4-km Joshimath-Auli Ropeway One of the Longest in Asia
Uttarakhand.subcategory: High Himalayan Alpine Meadow & Winter Ski Resort
Uttarakhand.description: An awe-inspiring Himalayan alpine meadow (bugyal) situated at an elevation of 2,500 to 3,050 meters in the Garhwal Himalayas. Regarded as India's premier ski destination, Auli offers breathtaking 360-degree views of sacred peaks including Nanda Devi (7,816 m), Kamet, Trishul, and Mana Parvat. Connected to Joshimath via a 4-km cable car—one of the highest ropeways in Asia—the meadow transforms from wildflower carpets in summer into world-class powder ski slopes in winter.
Uttarakhand.entryFee: Free access to meadow; Joshimath-Auli Cable Car ₹1000 round trip
Uttarakhand.bestTimeToVisit: December to March (Skiing & Snow) | May to October (Lush Green Bugyal)
subtypes: High Himalayan Alpine Meadow & Winter Ski Resort
Uttarakhand.imageAlt: Snow-draped alpine ski slopes of Auli facing the towering Nanda Devi Himalayan peaks
highlights: 360° Panoramas of India's Highest Peaks (Nanda Devi, Trishul, Kamet)
4-km Joshimath-Auli Ropeway One of the Longest in Asia
World's Highest Artificial Snow-Making Lake at 3,000m
Winter International Ski Federation (FIS) Approved Slopes

Uttarakhand.name: Nainital Lake (Naini Tal) & Naina Devi Teertham
alternateNames: Sacred Crescent Lake where Sati's Eye Fell (Shakti Peeth)
Maa Naina Devi Temple on the Picturesque Northern Shore
Uttarakhand.subcategory: Sacred Crescent Hill-Station Lake & Shakti Peeth
Uttarakhand.description: A natural freshwater crescent lake situated at an elevation of 1,938 meters in the Kumaon foothills, encircled by seven verdant pine-clad hills. Revered in the Skanda Purana as Tri-Rishi Sarovar and as the holy Shakti Peeth where Goddess Sati's emerald eye ('Naina') fell. Boasts colorful rowing yachts along Mall Road, the ancient Maa Naina Devi Temple on its northern bank, and Naina Peak (2,615 m) offering sweeping vistas of the snowbound Great Himalayas.
Uttarakhand.timings: Boating: 06:00 AM - 06:00 PM | Promenade & Temple: 06:00 AM - 09:00 PM
Uttarakhand.entryFee: Free access to lake and temple; Rowing boat ₹210 - ₹350 per round
Uttarakhand.bestTimeToVisit: March to June & September to November
subtypes: Sacred Crescent Hill-Station Lake & Shakti Peeth
Uttarakhand.imageAlt: Emerald waters of crescent Nainital lake surrounded by misty pine-covered Kumaon mountains
highlights: Sacred Crescent Lake where Sati's Eye Fell (Shakti Peeth)
Maa Naina Devi Temple on the Picturesque Northern Shore
Vintage Rowing Boats & Yachting Under Pine Ridge Cliffs
Naina Peak (2,615 m) Panoramic View of Great Himalayan Range

Uttarakhand.name: Kedarkantha Summit Trek (12,500 ft Himalayan Snow Peak)
Uttarakhand.subcategory: Alpine Winter Snow Summit Trek (12,500 ft)
Uttarakhand.description: Starting from the picturesque pine village of Sankri inside Govind Pashu Vihar National Park, Kedarkantha is one of India's most celebrated winter summit treks. Climbing through dense oak forests and open snowfields to a pointed rocky crest adorned with a stone Trishul shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, yielding a 360-degree vista of Swargarohini, Black Peak, and Bandarpoonch.
Uttarakhand.imageAlt: Panoramic snow-covered mountain ridges and Shiva trishul at Kedarkantha summit, Uttarakhand
highlights: Juda Ka Talab Frozen Alpine Lake

Uttarakhand.name: Tehri Dam & High Altitude Reservoir (India's Tallest Dam)
alternateNames: India's Tallest Dam Engineering Marvel (260.5 m)
Uttarakhand.description: Standing at a height of 260.5 meters on the Bhagirathi River in the Garhwal Himalayas, Tehri Dam is the tallest dam in India and one of the highest earth-and-rockfill dams in the world. Its vast 52 sq km emerald alpine reservoir ('Tehri Lake') is surrounded by Himalayan peaks and is a premier hub for water sports and jet skiing.
Uttarakhand.bestTimeToVisit: March to June, September to December
Uttarakhand.imageAlt: Vast turquoise blue mountain lake enclosed by steep Himalayan ridge lines at Tehri Dam
highlights: India's Tallest Dam Engineering Marvel (260.5 m)
Tehri Lake Water Sports & Floating Huts
New Tehri Planned Himalayan Hill Town

Chandigarh.name: Rock Garden by Nek Chand
Chandigarh.description: A globally renowned 40-acre sculpture garden created secretly by Nek Chand Saini over 18 years, built entirely of industrial, domestic waste, and discarded ceramics (broken bangles, porcelain sinks, electrical sockets, tiles) transforming into whimsical courtyards and waterfalls.
Chandigarh.imageAlt: Whimsical open-air amphitheater and mosaic sculptures created from recycled ceramic, Chandigarh

Tripura.name: Unakoti Rock-Cut Carvings & Shaivite Pilgrimage
Tripura.description: An ancient Shaivite rock-cut pilgrimage hill in Tripura, featuring thousands of colossal bas-relief stone sculptures carved into the forested hillside. The central 30-foot carving of Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava is crowned by a colossal 10-foot headdress and flanked by Goddess Ganga riding a makara.
Tripura.bestTimeToVisit: October to March (Ashokastami Mela in April)
Tripura.imageAlt: Giant 30-foot bas-relief stone head of Lord Shiva (Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava) carved into forest rock

Uttar Pradesh.name: Kachori Gali & Blue Lassi Chowk, Varanasi
Uttar Pradesh.description: Narrow medieval stone labyrinth just meters from Manikarnika Ghat and Kashi Vishwanath. Famed for century-old halwais frying piping hot hing-kachoris in desi ghee served with aloo-tamatar sabzi and sweet jalebis, paired with clay-kulhad hand-churned fruit lassi.

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh State Tourism & Statutory Gazetteer

Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: Fresh crisp hing kachoris being fried hot in copper vessels inside the ancient lanes of Varanasi

Uttar Pradesh.name: Taj Mahal (UNESCO World Heritage)
Uttar Pradesh.subcategory: Mughal White Marble Mausoleum & World Wonder
Uttar Pradesh.description: An immense mausoleum of white Makrana marble, built in Agra between 1631 and 1648 by order of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Celebrated globally as the jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage, featuring exquisite Pietra Dura floral inlay, 43-meter minarets, and Persian Charbagh formal gardens along the Yamuna riverfront.
Uttar Pradesh.timings: Sunrise to Sunset (Closed on Fridays for prayers)
Uttar Pradesh.entryFee: ₹50 (Indian citizens), ₹1100 (Foreign tourists) + ₹200 optional for Main Mausoleum chamber
subtypes: Mughal White Marble Mausoleum & World Wonder
Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: The Taj Mahal reflecting symmetrically in the Yamuna Charbagh fountain pool at sunrise, Agra

Uttar Pradesh.name: Tomb of I'timad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
Uttar Pradesh.subcategory: Pietra Dura Marble Mausoleum & Jewel Box Tomb
Uttar Pradesh.description: Often described as a 'jewel box' and regarded as a draft of the Taj Mahal, this elegant tomb was commissioned by Empress Nur Jahan between 1622 and 1628 for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg. Built entirely from white Rajasthani marble encrusted with semi-precious stone Pietra Dura, it marks the historic architectural transition from red sandstone to white marble in Mughal architecture.
subtypes: Pietra Dura Marble Mausoleum & Jewel Box Tomb
Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: Intricate Pietra Dura marble lattice and facade of the Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daulah, Agra

Uttar Pradesh.name: Agra Fort (UNESCO World Heritage)
Uttar Pradesh.description: A colossal 16th-century Mughal red sandstone fortress founded by Emperor Akbar on the banks of the Yamuna River. Enclosed by 2.5-km double battlements, this imperial city served as the main residence of the emperors of the Mughal Dynasty until 1638. Houses Jahangiri Mahal, Khas Mahal, Sheesh Mahal, and Musamman Burj where Shah Jahan spent his final years gazing at the Taj Mahal.
subtypes: Imperial Mughal Red Sandstone Citadel
Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: Amar Singh Gate and imposing red sandstone ramparts of Agra Fort, Uttar Pradesh
highlights: Musamman Burj Taj Mahal River Vista

Uttar Pradesh.name: Fatehpur Sikri Imperial Complex (UNESCO)
alternateNames: White Marble Dargah of Sheikh Salim Chishti
Uttar Pradesh.description: The fortified ghost capital founded by Emperor Akbar in 1571 CE atop a rocky ridge 37 km west of Agra. Preserves the finest ensemble of unified Mughal architecture, anchored by the colossal 54-meter Buland Darwaza (Gate of Magnificence), the white marble Dargah of Sufi Saint Sheikh Salim Chishti, the 5-tiered Panch Mahal pavilion, and the Diwan-i-Khas with its iconic carved central pillar.
subtypes: Mughal Ceremonial Capital & Buland Darwaza
Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: The monumental 54-meter Buland Darwaza gate at Fatehpur Sikri complex, Uttar Pradesh
highlights: White Marble Dargah of Sheikh Salim Chishti

Uttar Pradesh.name: Mehtab Bagh (Moonlight Garden)
alternateNames: Direct Axis Reflection of the Taj Mahal
Uttar Pradesh.description: The last of eleven Mughal-built gardens along the Yamuna River, located directly north of the Taj Mahal complex across the river. Perfectly aligned with the Taj Mahal, this 25-acre symmetrical Charbagh complex was designed by Emperor Babur and later restored by Emperor Shah Jahan as an ideal moonlight viewing pleasure garden, offering an unobstructed, crowd-free reflection of the marble wonder at sunset.
subtypes: Mughal Riverfront Charbagh Garden
Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: Mehtab Bagh formal Mughal gardens with symmetric view of the Taj Mahal across River Yamuna
highlights: Direct Axis Reflection of the Taj Mahal

Uttar Pradesh.name: Varanasi Banarasi Silk & Zari Weavers Quarter (GI Certified)
alternateNames: Pure Gold & Silver Zari Brocade Weaving
Uttar Pradesh.subcategory: GI Certified Handloom Silk & Zari Craft Cluster
Uttar Pradesh.description: Operating continuously in the winding mohallas of Madanpura, Peeli Kothi, and Chowk for centuries, the Banarasi handloom cluster crafts India's most prestigious bridal and ceremonial brocades. Using fine mulberry silk and gold or silver metallic thread (Zari), master weavers create intricate floral jal, paisley motifs, and mina work on jacquard and pit looms.

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh State Tourism & Statutory Gazetteer

Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: Intricate gold zari brocade pattern on handloom Banarasi red silk saree
highlights: Pure Gold & Silver Zari Brocade Weaving
GI Tag Certified Banarasi Silk Guilds

Uttar Pradesh.name: Lucknow Chowk Awadhi Culinary Precinct (Nawabi Heritage Corridor)
Uttar Pradesh.subcategory: Nawabi Awadhi Culinary Street & Kabab Heritage
Uttar Pradesh.description: The historic Chowk and Aminabad quarters of Lucknow are the custodians of royal Awadhi dum pukht culinary traditions cultivated under the Nawabs of Awadh. Famous worldwide for mouth-melting Galawati Kababs created at Tunday Kababi (est. 1905), slow-cooked saffron Sheermal flatbreads, and winter delicacy Makhan Malai (Nimish).

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh State Tourism & Statutory Gazetteer

Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: Tender Galawati Kababs sizzling on large circular copper tawa in historic Lucknow Chowk

Uttar Pradesh.name: Sarnath Dhamek Stupa & Deer Park (Dharmachakra Pravartana)
alternateNames: Dhamek Stupa (Turning the Wheel of Law)
Uttar Pradesh.description: Located 10 km northeast of Varanasi, Sarnath is where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) to his first five disciples in 528 BCE. The massive cylindrical Dhamek Stupa stands 43.6 meters high and 28 meters in diameter, marking the exact spot of the turning of the Wheel of Law, adorned with delicate 5th-century Gupta stone floral carving.
Uttar Pradesh.asiMonumentId: ASI Patna Circle Centrally Protected Monument

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India Gazette
sources.officialRecordId: ASI Patna Circle Centrally Protected Monument

Uttar Pradesh.imageAlt: Towering ancient stone cylinder of Dhamek Stupa surrounded by monastic brick foundations at Sarnath
highlights: Dhamek Stupa (Turning the Wheel of Law)

Punjab.name: Kesar Da Dhaba, Amritsar
Punjab.description: Established in 1916, this legendary dhaba in Chowk Passian cooks its black urad dal (Maa ki Dal) over slow smoldering charcoal for 12 continuous hours with pure desi ghee, served with multi-layered crisp laccha parathas.
Punjab.imageAlt: Legendary slow-cooked black urad dal makhani with crisp tandoori paratha at Kesar Da Dhaba

Punjab.name: Sri Harmandir Sahib (The Golden Temple & Supreme Sikh Takht)
Punjab.description: The spiritual and cultural center of the Sikh religion, founded in 1577 CE by Guru Ram Das Ji. The gold-plated sanctum rises from the sacred Amrit Sarovar pool and has four entrances welcoming all humanity without distinction of caste, religion, or gender. Houses the eternal Guru Granth Sahib and operates the world's largest community kitchen (Langar), serving over 100,000 free hot vegetarian meals daily.
Punjab.imageAlt: Glistening illuminated gold facade of Sri Harmandir Sahib reflected in the Amrit Sarovar pool at night
highlights: World's Largest Free Community Kitchen (Guru Ka Langar)
Akal Takht (Supreme Seat of Sikh Authority)

Punjab.name: Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial (Sacred Freedom Sanctuary)
alternateNames: Flame of Liberty Red Sandstone Memorial Spire
Punjab.description: A public garden spanning six to seven acres enclosed by brick walls, forever etched in Indian history as the site of the brutal 13 April 1919 massacre where General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire upon unarmed peaceful gathering celebrating Baisakhi. Features the preserved Martyrs' Well (Shahidi Khuh), bullet marks preserved in red brick walls, and the Flame of Liberty eternal torch monument.
Punjab.imageAlt: Red sandstone Flame of Liberty memorial tower surrounded by peaceful memorial lawns at Jallianwala Bagh
highlights: Flame of Liberty Red Sandstone Memorial Spire
Bullet Holes Preserved on Historic Brick Enclosure Walls
Interactive Light & Sound Freedom Struggle Memorial

Haryana.name: Brahma Sarovar & Jyotisar (Gita Birthplace)
alternateNames: Immortal Banyan Tree (Akshay Vat) at Jyotisar
Haryana.description: One of the most expansive sacred water tanks in Asia, measuring 1,800 by 1,400 feet, revered in the Mahabharata as created by Lord Brahma. Paired with Jyotisar, the hallowed spot beneath an immortal banyan tree where Lord Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna.
Haryana.bestTimeToVisit: October to March (Gita Jayanti in December)
Haryana.imageAlt: Vast serene stepped water tanks and evening diya lamps at sacred Brahma Sarovar, Kurukshetra
highlights: Immortal Banyan Tree (Akshay Vat) at Jyotisar

Jharkhand.name: Parasnath Hill (Shikharji Jain Maha Teerth)
Jharkhand.subcategory: Highest Peak in Jharkhand & Supreme Jain Kshetra
Jharkhand.description: The highest mountain peak in Jharkhand at 1,365 meters. Known as Sammed Shikharji, the supreme sacred pilgrimage destination of Jainism, where twenty of the twenty-four Tirthankaras attained Nirvana. Pilgrims undertake the reverent 27 km mountain parikrama circumambulating the hilltop tonks.
Jharkhand.timings: Open 24 hours (Pilgrims start parikrama at 03:00 AM)
Jharkhand.imageAlt: Sacred tonks and Jain marble shrines crowning the highest mountain peak in Jharkhand, Shikharji

Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.name: Diu Fort & Monolithic Naida Caves
alternateNames: Labyrinthine Naida Rock Caves with Light Beams
Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.description: Monumental 16th-century coastal fortress built on the Arabian Sea, featuring stone ramparts with antique Portuguese cannons overlooking the sea. Adjoined by Naida Caves, a labyrinthine system of ancient sandstone grottoes carved by nature and Portuguese quarrying with sunlight streaming through open rock roofs.

Mizoram.name: Vantawng Falls (Tallest Waterfall in Mizoram)
Mizoram.description: The highest uninterrupted waterfall in Mizoram with a total height of 229 meters (751 feet). Surging down amidst dense bamboo groves and evergreen tropical rainforest on the Vanva River near Thenzawl, revered in Mizo folklore.
Mizoram.imageAlt: Spectacular 750-foot plume cascading down lush tropical mountain walls of Vanva river, Mizoram

Mizoram.name: Phawngpui Blue Mountain & National Park
Mizoram.description: Revered as the 'Blue Mountain' and the sacred abode of the local folk deities, Phawngpui is the highest mountain peak in Mizoram at 2,157 meters. Overlooking the Chhimtuipui River and Myanmar border cliffs, famous for wild orchids, rhododendrons, and the rare Blyth's tragopan.
Mizoram.imageAlt: Misty pine cliffs and blooming rhododendron trees atop Phawngpui Blue Mountain Peak, Mizoram

Nagaland.name: Dzukou Valley & Lily Sanctuary
Nagaland.description: Perched at 2,452 meters along the border of Nagaland and Manipur. Known as the 'Valley of Flowers of the Northeast', renowned for its rolling dwarf-bamboo green hills, meandering natural streams, and the endemic Dzukou Lily (Lilium chitrangadae) found nowhere else on Earth.
Nagaland.bestTimeToVisit: June to September (Dzukou Lily bloom) & October to March
Nagaland.imageAlt: Rolling green undulating knolls and crystal brook meandering through Dzukou Valley, Nagaland

Nagaland.name: Kisama Naga Heritage Village (Hornbill Festival)
Nagaland.subcategory: Indigenous Naga Tribal Architecture & Living Arts
Nagaland.description: Designed as an authentic amphitheater of living Naga culture near Kohima. Features traditional wood-carved morungs (dormitories) representing the 16 recognized tribes of Nagaland, traditional totemic gateposts, and host of the globally celebrated annual Hornbill Festival every December.
Nagaland.bestTimeToVisit: December (Hornbill Festival 1st-10th Dec) & October to April
Nagaland.imageAlt: Intricate wooden totems and traditional thatched morung houses at Kisama Heritage Village, Kohima

Nagaland.name: Khonoma Green Village (India's First Green Village & Angami Heritage)
alternateNames: India's First Community Green Village Project
Nagaland.subcategory: First Community Nature Conservation Sanctuary & Naga Village
Nagaland.description: Perched on mist-draped terraced hills 20 km from Kohima, Khonoma is inhabited by the Angami Naga tribe and is officially recognized as India's first green village. Celebrated for banning logging and commercial hunting, creating the 20 sq km Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary, traditional carved Morungs (youth dormitories), and stone forts that resisted British troops in 1879.
Nagaland.imageAlt: Tiered green paddy terraces on mist-covered hills leading to stone village gate at Khonoma, Nagaland
highlights: India's First Community Green Village Project
Angami Naga Traditional Morungs & Stone Fortresses

Sikkim.name: Gurudongmar Sacred Lake (17,800 ft)
Sikkim.description: One of the highest lakes in the world at an altitude of 5,430 meters (17,800 ft) in North Sikkim near the Tibetan border. Revered as deeply sacred by Buddhists, Sikhs, and Hindus, blessed by Guru Padmasambhava and Guru Nanak so that a central portion of the lake never freezes even during sub-zero winters.
Sikkim.timings: 07:00 AM - 01:00 PM (Requires army permit and early return due to winds)
Sikkim.bestTimeToVisit: April to June & October to November
Sikkim.imageAlt: Sacred alpine glacial lake at 17,800 feet reflecting pristine snow peaks, North Sikkim

Sikkim.name: Tsomgo Lake & Nathu La Pass (Old Silk Route)
alternateNames: Nathu La Border Trading Post (14,140 ft)
Sikkim.description: A sacred high-altitude glacial lake at 3,753 meters (12,313 ft) in East Sikkim, reflecting changing water colors with the seasons. Connected along the historic Old Silk Route to the historic Nathu La Pass (14,140 ft) on the Indo-China border and the revered Baba Harbhajan Singh Memorial Temple.
Sikkim.bestTimeToVisit: March to May (Rhododendron blooms) & October to December
Sikkim.imageAlt: Glacial alpine waters of oval Tsomgo Lake nestled in steep mountain slopes, East Sikkim
highlights: Nathu La Border Trading Post (14,140 ft)
